We performed sensitivity studies simulating operation under each of the controllers. Throughout these simulations, we varied the design of the DER—battery storage and solar PV—and evaluated the controllers’ performance against a baseline. In addition to quantifying the performance of the controllers, we used the results of these tests to identify appropriate DER configurations, which were used in the CHIL emulations presented in Section 5. The DER configurations selected for the CHIL tests provide a reasonable balance between the two objectives to satisfy EV charging needs and mitigate electrical upgrades. While the controllers were tested assuming different DER configurations, other case study parameters were consistent across simulations to provide an opportunity for direct comparison: • The normalized solar PV generation was fixed. Varying the amount of PV installed changed the amount of energy produced but not the normalized power profile. • The EV charging sessions (i.e., trips) were also fixed. Each session represents a vehicle being dropped off at the RCC and is defined by vehicle type, which in turn dictates charge acceptance profile and battery capacity, arrival time, drop-off SOC, and vehicle dwell time. The simulation included 750 charge sessions in a 24-hour span. • The SOC at which vehicles are given to customers—also referred to as target or pickup SOC—was fixed at 80%. • The number of charging ports by type was also kept constant across scenarios: 277 EVSE at 25 kW and 21 EVSE at 350 kW of charging capacity each. These numbers were selected because in an ideal scenario—where all vehicles’ charging requirements and dwell times are known in advance—they represent the minimum infrastructure required for no queueing at the EVSE. • The facility load profile was provided by Dallas Fort Worth International Airport and reflects what was measured by the utility meter at the RCC. • The grid capacity ceiling, which is the maximum power that can be drawn at the utility feeder, was limited to 2 MW, reflecting anecdotal information about the airport’s RCC.
